quickSummary: The prokaryotic cell envelope consists of an outer Glycocalyx (loose slime layer or rigid antiphagocytic capsule), a Peptidoglycan cell wall (thick in Gram+, thin with outer LPS membrane in Gram-), and an inner selectively permeable plasma membrane. Membranous invaginations form Mesosomes (respiration, DNA replication) and Chromatophores. Appendages include Flagella (locomotion), Pili (conjugation bridge), and Fimbriae (attachment). Non-membranous inclusion bodies store phosphate, protein, glycogen, and gas.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2. The Three-Layered Cell Envelope
conceptBreakdown.title: 2. The Three-Layered Cell Envelope

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Envelope = Glycocalyx (protective capsule/slime) + Peptidoglycan cell wall (osmotic barrier) + Plasma membrane (transport & mesosomes).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PROKARYOTIC CELL ENVELOPE LAYERS
                                        │
         ┌──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                              ▼                              ▼
    GLYCOCALYX                      CELL WALL                   PLASMA MEMBRANE
(Capsule or Slime Layer)       (Peptidoglycan Layer)         (Phospholipid Bilayer)
 ├── Protection from Phagocytosis ├── Prevents Osmotic Lysis   ├── Selective Permeability
 └── Surface Adhesion             └── Gram+ vs Gram- Staining  └── Invaginates to Mesosomes
conceptBreakdown.content:
Prokaryotic cells possess a complex, three-layered chemically protective envelope acting as a single coordinated structural unit:

1. **Glycocalyx**: Outermost polymeric coat.
   - **Slime Layer**: Loose, non-rigid gelatinous polysaccharide layer preventing desiccation and nutrient loss.
   - **Capsule**: Thick, rigid, organized polysaccharide or poly-D-glutamic acid coat protecting pathogens (*e.g., Streptococcus pneumoniae*) from host immune phagocytosis.
2. **Cell Wall**: Intermediate rigid layer preventing osmotic bursting or collapse.
   - **Gram-Positive**: Thick peptidoglycan ($20\text{--}80\text{ nm}$) infused with teichoic and lipoteichoic acids.
   - **Gram-Negative**: Thin peptidoglycan ($2\text{--}7\text{ nm}$) bounded by an outer membrane containing Lipopolysaccharide (LPS / Endotoxin) and porin channels.
3. **Plasma Membrane**: Innermost selectively permeable lipid bilayer.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Mesosomes & Photosynthetic Chromatophores
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Mesosomes & Photosynthetic Chromatophores
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Mesosomes**: Specialized invaginations of the plasma membrane into vesicles, tubules, or lamellae. They increase membrane surface area and enzymatic capacity, performing:
  1. Cellular respiration (housing respiratory ETC enzymes).
  2. Cell wall synthesis.
  3. DNA replication and equal distribution of chromosomes to daughter cells.
• **Chromatophores**: Pigment-containing membranous internal lamellae in photosynthetic bacteria (*cyanobacteria, purple/green sulfur bacteria*).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### Bacterial Surface Appendages
• **Flagella**: Locomotory helical appendages composed of **Flagellin** protein, divided into Basal Body (motor), Hook, and Filament.
• **Pili**: Elongated tubular protein structures composed of **Pilin**; the **Sex Pilus** forms a conjugation bridge during bacterial parasexual gene transfer ($F^+ \times F^-$).
• **Fimbriae**: Small, bristle-like fibrous appendages that allow bacteria to adhere to rocks in streams and to host mucosal epithelial tissues.

### Non-Membranous Inclusion Bodies
• **Phosphate Granules (Volutin / Metachromatic granules)**: Stores inorganic polyphosphate.
• **Cyanophycean Granules**: Stores structured reserve proteins (arginine and aspartic acid polymers).
• **Glycogen Granules**: Stores glucose polymers.
• **Gas Vacuoles**: Proteinaceous hollow cylindrical membranes permeable to metabolic gases but impermeable to water, providing buoyancy in cyanobacteria and purple/green sulfur bacteria.
